2027-03-19.title: The Fortieth Friday · Mar Yauseph (St Joseph)
readings: Jesus fasts forty days and is tempted
David will not offer what costs him nothing
Amend your ways and your doings
Ransomed with the precious blood of Christ
Whether we live or die, we are the Lord's
Joseph did as the angel commanded
2027-03-19.alt: The Fortieth Friday: the forty days of the Great Fast (Valiya Nombu) are completed today. Also the feast of Mar Yauseph (St Joseph), spouse of the Virgin Mary, with its own readings (Romans 4:16–18; Matthew 1:18–25). The Panchangam notes that there is no fasting and no forty prostrations (kumbideel) today. Tomorrow is Lazarus Saturday, and Sunday is Hosanna Sunday: remind the faithful to bring palm leaves and flowers.
2027-03-19.verse: One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.
theo: Today the forty days are complete. Since Shubkono on 8 February the Church has fasted, prayed and made her prostrations, walking with the Lord who “fasted forty days and forty nights, and afterwards he was famished.” The Panchangam sets side by side two scenes of temptation. In a garden full of fruit the serpent asks, “Did God say…?” and promises, “You will not die… you will be like God.” The woman sees that the tree is “good for food,” “a delight to the eyes,” and “to be desired to make one wise”; she takes and eats, and gives to her husband. In a desert without bread the same tempter comes to Jesus with the same three hungers: for bread, for display, for power. Where Adam doubted the word of God, Jesus answers each time with that word: “It is written, ‘One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.’” St Irenaeus taught that the Lord fought as a man against the enemy who had taken us captive in Adam, and conquered him, so that what was lost at a tree in a garden was won back in obedience (in substance). Luke adds a sober line: “When the devil had finished every test, he departed from him until an opportune time.” That time will come in Gethsemane and on the Cross.

The other readings ask what our fast has been for. Isaiah hears the people complain, “Why do we fast, but you do not see?” and God answers: “Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice… Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house?” Jeremiah, at the Temple gate, warns against trusting in holy places while living unholy lives: “Amend your ways and your doings, and let me dwell with you in this place.” David, buying the threshing floor where the Temple would later stand, refuses a free gift: “I will not offer burnt offerings to the Lord my God that cost me nothing.” And Peter shows us the price of our own redemption: “not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without defect or blemish.” So Paul can say: “If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord; so then, whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord’s.” The forty days end today, but the Fast is not over: tomorrow we stand at the tomb of Lazarus, and on Sunday we enter Jerusalem with the Lord and begin the Week of the Passion.

This year the Fortieth Friday falls on the feast of Mar Yauseph, St Joseph, and so the Church does not fast or make the prostrations today. Joseph is the right companion for this day. Like Abraham, of whom Paul writes, “Hoping against hope, he believed,” Joseph trusted God's word when nothing made sense. Finding Mary with child, “being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace,” he planned to dismiss her quietly. Then the angel spoke in a dream: “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.” And Matthew gives the whole of Joseph in one line: “When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him.” Where Adam heard God's word and doubted it, Joseph heard and obeyed at once, without a single recorded word. Pope Francis, in Patris Corde, called him a father in the shadows, beloved, tender, obedient, accepting, creatively courageous and a working man (in substance). The guardian of the Child in Bethlehem stood near the Mother at the beginning of the road that ends at Calvary. On the last day of the Forty, we ask him to guard the Church as he guarded the Holy Family.
outline: Ask: what has the Fast changed in me in these forty days?
Adam doubts the word; Christ conquers with it.
Point 2 · The fast that I choose
Mercy, amendment, a sacrifice that costs, the precious blood.
Point 3 · Joseph did as the angel commanded
“One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.”
live: Choose one verse from today's readings and learn it by heart; say it whenever temptation comes this Holy Week.
Before Sunday, give what you saved by fasting during these forty days to someone who is hungry or homeless.
Do at once one thing you know God has been asking of you, without waiting for a better time.
2027-03-19.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, for forty days and forty nights you fasted in the wilderness and overcame the tempter by the word of God, where our first parents fell. Thank you for bringing us to the end of these forty days. Let our fast bear fruit in mercy to the hungry, in amended lives, and in offerings that cost us something, for you have ransomed us with your precious blood. By the prayers of Mar Yauseph, the righteous man who did at once what the Lord commanded, give us silent and ready obedience, guard our families, and lead us with you into Jerusalem, to your Cross and your Resurrection. Amen.
altar: We were ransomed “not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ”; that blood, the price of our redemption, is offered and given on the altar.

quick: The forty days are complete: Jesus conquers with the word of God the tempter who overcame Adam.
The fast God chooses is mercy, amendment of life, and an offering that costs; we were ransomed by the precious blood of Christ.
St Joseph, a righteous man, did at once what the angel of the Lord commanded.
2027-03-19.action: Give today what you saved by fasting during these forty days.
2027-03-19.question: Where did I fall in these forty days, and where did the word of God help me stand?
2027-03-19.special: The Fortieth Friday and the feast of Mar Yauseph (St Joseph): no fasting and no forty prostrations today (Panchangam). Announce Lazarus Saturday (20 Mar) and Hosanna Sunday (21 Mar); remind the faithful to bring palm leaves and flowers.

family.explain: Today the forty days of the Great Fast are finished. Jesus fasted forty days, and when the devil tempted him, Jesus answered with words from the Bible. Today is also the feast of St Joseph. When the angel told Joseph what to do, he got up and did it at once. Jesus and Joseph both listened to God's word.
family.intention: We pray for all fathers, and for families that are struggling.
family.ask: Ask: “What did our family give up or do in these forty days, and what did we learn?”

illus: A rubber tapper near Ranni rose at four every morning for thirty-eight years. He spoke little. When his wife fell ill he took over the cooking without a complaint; when his son failed an examination he said only, we will try again. At his funeral the parish priest asked the children what they remembered most. The eldest daughter said: I never once heard him raise his voice, and I never once saw him miss his evening prayer. The priest said: then you have seen something of St Joseph.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you fasted forty days and overcame the tempter by the word of God. Thank you for these forty days. With Mar Yauseph, teach us to hear and obey. Amen.
share: The tree was good for food, a delight to the eyes (Genesis 3:6). Which of the three hungers most often tempts me: comfort, display or power?
Is not this the fast that I choose: to share your bread with the hungry? (Isaiah 58:6–7). Has my fast reached the poor?
He did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). What is God asking me to do now, without delay?
pm.resp: Lord, lead us not into temptation.
interc: In thanksgiving for the forty days of the Great Fast, and for all who kept it faithfully.
For fathers and foster fathers, for carpenters and all who work with their hands, through the prayers of St Joseph.
For all who are tempted to despair, addiction or dishonesty, that they may stand firm by the word of God.
For the hungry and the homeless, that our fasting may become their bread.
For our parishes as we prepare for Lazarus Saturday, Hosanna Sunday and the Week of the Passion.
pm.close: Father, your Son conquered the tempter in the wilderness, and Joseph, the righteous man, obeyed your word in silence. Let our forty days bear fruit in mercy and obedience, and bring us with your Son through his Passion to the joy of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the forty days of the Great Fast are complete. Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights, and the devil came to tempt him. Long ago, in a garden full of fruit, our first parents listened to the tempter and doubted God's word (Genesis 3:1–6). In a desert without bread, Jesus answered: One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God (Matthew 4:4).

What was our fast for? Isaiah tells us: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice… to share your bread with the hungry? (Isaiah 58:6–7). David said: I will not offer burnt offerings to the Lord my God that cost me nothing (2 Samuel 24:24). And Peter reminds us what our salvation cost: not silver or gold, but the precious blood of Christ (1 Peter 1:18–19).

Today is also the feast of St Joseph, so we do not fast today. Joseph is a man of few words and quick obedience. When the angel spoke to him in a dream, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him (Matthew 1:24). Adam heard God's word and doubted; Joseph heard and obeyed.

The forty days end, but our journey goes on. Tomorrow we stand with Martha and Mary at the tomb of Lazarus; on Sunday we wave palms and go up to Jerusalem with the Lord. Let us ask St Joseph to walk with us as he walked with Mary and the Child. Whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord's (Romans 14:8). Amen.
kids: Children, when the devil tempted Jesus, Jesus answered with words from the Bible. You can do the same: when you feel like lying or being unkind, say a Bible word, like: Jesus, I love you more. And St Joseph, whose feast is today, did what God asked right away. Can you obey your parents right away today, like Joseph?

intro: The epistle for Mar Yauseph speaks of Abraham, who hoping against hope believed. Joseph walked the same road of faith in the dark.

points.apply: When someone disappoints you this week, choose not to expose them.

sub: Faith trusts God's word in the night.
points.apply: Bring to God one situation where you see no way forward.

points.h: He took Mary into his home
points.apply: Do at once one good thing you know God is asking of you.

concl: Joseph believed when he could not see, and obeyed before he understood.
His faith made a home for Mary and for the Son of God.
opts.resolve: When I cannot understand God's ways this week, I will trust like Joseph and obey at once.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this Fortieth Friday we keep the feast of Mar Yauseph, Saint Joseph. The Church gives us for his feast a passage about Abraham: hoping against hope, he believed that he would become the father of many nations (Romans 4:18). Abraham believed when everything he could see said no. Joseph lived the same faith.

Think of the moment when he learned that Mary was with child. He did not yet know that the child was from the Holy Spirit. Saint Matthew tells us: her husband Joseph, being a righteous man and unwilling to expose her to public disgrace, planned to dismiss her quietly (Matthew 1:19). In his pain he still chose mercy. The prophet Micah said what God asks: to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God (Micah 6:8). Joseph did all three.

Then God spoke in a dream: Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit (Matthew 1:20). God had promised David a son whose kingdom would last for ever (2 Samuel 7:12–16). Now that promise passed through the obedience of a carpenter. Joseph did not ask for proof. When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife (Matthew 1:24).

This is what hoping against hope looks like. Not a feeling, but a decision to trust God's word when we cannot see the way. Many of us carry a situation like Joseph's: a family problem, an illness, a worry about our children, a future that is dark. Joseph teaches us to bring it to God, to choose mercy, and to obey the next thing God shows us.

The forty days are complete, and Holy Week is near. Let us ask Mar Yauseph to give us his faith: a faith that does not demand to understand everything, but takes Mary and Jesus into its home and walks on. And at the Holy Qurbono today let us offer God the situation where we see no way forward. Amen.

opts.a: Go to Joseph: the guardian of the Redeemer
intro: In Egypt, Pharaoh said to the hungry people: Go to Joseph. The Church has long applied these words to Saint Joseph, the guardian of the Holy Family and of the whole Church.

sub: He protects the Church as he protected Jesus.
points.apply: Entrust your family's safety and needs to Saint Joseph tonight.

sub: Not one word of his is recorded.
points.apply: Offer your daily work to God each morning this week.

sub: Tradition holds that he died with Jesus and Mary beside him.
Whether we live or die, we are the Lord's.
points.apply: Pray each night for a holy death, for yourself and for the dying.

concl: Joseph guarded the Redeemer with his strength, his work and his silence.
He still guards the Church and stands beside the dying.
opts.resolve: This week I will entrust my family and my work to Saint Joseph, and pray each night for a holy death.
homily: Dear friends, in the book of Genesis, when famine came upon Egypt, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said: go to Joseph; what he says to you, do (Genesis 41:55). That Joseph kept the grain that saved his family and the nations. The Church has long seen in him a picture of our Joseph, Mar Yauseph, to whom God entrusted the Bread of Life himself.

Joseph was first of all a guardian. When Herod wanted to kill the Child, the angel said: get up, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt (Matthew 2:13). He rose in the night and went. He did not protect Jesus with an army, but with his watchfulness, his strength and his readiness. That is why the Church calls him her protector. What he did for the body of Jesus in Nazareth, he does now for the body of Christ, which is the Church.

Joseph was also a worker. The people of Nazareth said of Jesus: is not this the carpenter's son? (Matthew 13:55). For years the Son of God learned a trade at Joseph's side. The Psalm says: you shall eat the fruit of the labor of your hands; you shall be happy (Psalm 128:2). The Gospels do not record a single word of Joseph. His holiness was in faithful, hidden, daily work.

Finally, Joseph is the patron of a holy death. The Gospels do not tell us when he died, but the tradition of the Church holds that he died with Jesus and Mary beside him. Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his faithful ones (Psalm 116:15). Today's epistle says: whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord's (Romans 14:8).

So let us go to Joseph. Let us entrust to him our families, our children's safety and our daily work. Let us offer our work each morning as he did. And each night let us ask for the grace of a holy death, with Jesus and Mary beside us, and pray for those who will die tonight. Amen.

intro: Theme: “One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.”
On the Fortieth Friday and the feast of St Joseph: the tempter overcome, the fast God chooses, and the righteous man who obeyed.

sub: Adam doubts the word in a garden of plenty.
Christ answers with the word in a desert of hunger.
q: I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and hers; he will strike your head, and you will strike his heel.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin.
points.apply: Learn one verse by heart today and use it against temptation in Holy Week.

sub: An offering that costs; the precious blood.
q: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to undo the thongs of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke?

You know that you were ransomed from the futile ways inherited from your ancestors, not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without defect or blemish.
points.apply: Give what you saved in the forty days to the hungry before Sunday.

points.h: Joseph did as the angel commanded
sub: A righteous man, unwilling to shame.
q: Your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me; your throne shall be established forever.
When Joseph awoke from sleep, he did as the angel of the Lord commanded him; he took her as his wife,
points.apply: Do at once the one thing God has long been asking of you.

concl: The forty days end in the victory of the word over the tempter.
With St Joseph we go on, obedient and hoping, toward Lazarus, Jerusalem and the Cross.
2027-03-19.resolve: Live by every word from the mouth of God, and obey it at once, like Joseph.
